subject: Physiology
summary: Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) is released by atrial myocytes when the heart is stretched, promoting natriuresis, diuresis, vasodilation, and suppression of renin and ADH. It balances fluid and pressure homeostasis. Low levels contribute to heart failure and hypertension.

sections.p: ANP is a peptide hormone produced mainly by atrial cardiomyocytes. It is released when atrial wall tension rises, such as in volume overload. Its actions counteract the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system (RAAS) and antidiuretic hormone (ADH).

ANP binds natriuretic peptide receptors (NPR-A) on renal tubular cells, increasing intracellular cGMP. This leads to sodium excretion, water loss, and vasodilation. In the brain, ANP inhibits ADH release, reducing water reabsorption.

Atrial stretch is the primary trigger. Sympathetic tone, catecholamines, and circulating volume also modulate release. ANP levels rise in acute heart failure, hypertension, and volume expansion, and fall when volume normalises.
b: Levels rise in heart failure and hypertension

sections.p: Reduced ANP production or action occurs in chronic heart failure, obesity, and renal disease, leading to fluid retention and hypertension. Excessive ANP can cause hypotension and electrolyte disturbances.

t.b: Assess severity of heart failure; low in chronic HF, high in acute decompensation
Marker of ANP activity; low in low ANP states

sections.p: Measuring ANP or cGMP helps gauge heart failure severity and response to diuretics. Low ANP suggests inadequate compensatory response, guiding therapy intensification.

t.b: Differential diagnosis of dyspnoea; high in HF, low in pulmonary embolism
Assess natriuretic response; low indicates impaired ANP action

sections.p: Remember ANP counteracts RAAS and ADH, promotes natriuresis, diuresis, vasodilation. In heart failure, low ANP contributes to fluid overload. Distinguish from BNP, which is released from ventricles.
b: ANP vs BNP: atrial vs ventricular source

t.b: Which hormone is released from atria vs ventricles? BNP is ventricular

faq.q: Why does ANP decrease in chronic heart failure?
faq.a: Long‑term ventricular dilation reduces atrial stretch and ANP synthesis, and renal resistance to ANP increases.

faq.q: Can ANP levels be measured in low‑resource settings?
faq.a: Serum ANP assays are costly; cGMP or BNP can be used as surrogate markers when available.

faq.q: Does ANP affect blood pressure in hypertension?
faq.a: Yes, by vasodilation and natriuresis, ANP lowers systemic vascular resistance and volume, helping control hypertension.
